expert_role: LiDAR and GIS specialist (city-scale 3D context models, vertical datums, DEM fusion)

findings.item: C02-M05 R2 ring / dataset 'NRCan HRDEM by LiDAR project'
findings.issue: The plan relies on HRDEM BC-Lower_Mainland_2016-1m for the North Shore front ranges because its bbox reaches 49.5125 N. A bbox is not coverage. I tested the NRCan extent GeoJSON (BC-Lower_Mainland_2016-1m-extent.geojson). Grouse peak, Mount Seymour, Crown, Cypress and the Lions all fall outside it. Only downtown, the City of North Vancouver and Capilano Lake fall inside. BC-Vancouver_Island_Sunshine_Coast_2018 covers Hollyburn but none of the other peaks. NRCAN-Lower_Mainland_2019 covers none of them. The STAC extent for mosaic 2_3 is only a tile rectangle, so it proves nothing about coverage. As a result, the mountain profile lines that the protected views exist to protect (about 11 to 20 km away) probably have only GLO-30-derived MRDEM-30, with forest removal and roughly 5 m RMSE in vegetation by the spec's own numbers. That is not 1 m LiDAR.
findings.fix: Rewrite R2 around measured coverage. (1) Download each candidate's coverage.gpkg (mosaic 2_3 is 183 MB) or sample the mosaic COG at the peaks to find nodata. (2) Ask LidarBC (LiDAR@gov.bc.ca), Metro Vancouver (watershed LiDAR, held internally at 5 m) and the Districts of North and West Vancouver for North Shore LiDAR. (3) Until one of those arrives, label the mountain terrain 'MRDEM-30, GLO-30-derived, about 5 m RMSE forested' and change the 'HRDEM better than 1 m' metric so it applies only where coverage is confirmed.

findings.item: C02-M07 / flag 'Vista local frame is adequate'
findings.issue: The spec explains the gap between Vista and UTM as a generic frame difference that is 'fine for visuals'. The real cause is a wrong constant. Vista uses y = dlat x 110574, which is the metres per degree of latitude at the equator. At 49.28 N the GRS80 value is about 111,215, so north-south distances are 0.58% short. The supplied Rhino model matches this formula to 0.08 m (geo.json check points), so the supplied model itself carries the distortion. My computed offsets from UTM are -27.4 m N at (0, -5083), +21.3 m N at the north edge of the supplied model (0, 3940) and -33.6 m at the SE corner. The figure of 'about 5 m at 2.5 km' is for an east-west offset only.
findings.fix: Store every new layer in EPSG:3157. Treat Vista assets as a distorted legacy frame, with a documented forward/inverse transform (Vista formula, then lon/lat, then UTM). Run all M07 building-by-building comparisons in UTM after re-projecting Vista geometry with Vista's own formula. Fix Vista's constant (or move it to UTM) before any further cone-overlap work.

findings.issue: The City's 2022 LiDAR metadata names the geoid as the Metro Vancouver geoid HTMVBC00 (HTMVBC00_Abbbyn.zip), not HTGVRDBC00. GeoBC says the two are equivalent inside Metro Vancouver. LTSA 465C approves HTGVRDBC00, plus HTv2.0 at epoch 1997.0 outside Metro Vancouver. The PROJ grid the spec chooses, ca_nrc_HT2_2010v70_CGG2013a, is HTv2.0 at epoch 2010, so it differs from both the City's and the LTSA model in epoch and in hybrid realisation. Two more gaps: the MRDEM record says GLO-30 was converted with CGG2013, not CGG2013a, and the registry does not separate CGVD2013 from CGVD2013a(2010).
findings.fix: Record the geoid as HTMVBC00 (equivalent to HTGVRDBC00) and the epoch for every layer. Measure the CGVD28 to CGVD2013 relationship with a same-source pair instead of relying on the national grid: City DEM 2013 (CGVD28) against HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER 2013 (CGVD2013), both built from the same 2013 points, so their difference is the shift NRCan actually applied. Add a unit test that fixes the vgridshift sign (EPSG:10520 uses multiplier -1) against that pair.

findings.issue: A 'building-class above 2.5 m' mask merges touching downtown podiums, and the spec admits the mask merges touching buildings. Each mask component therefore covers a whole block, while the City polygons are split at parcel lines. IoU between one parcel polygon and a block component will fall below 0.7 for almost every downtown building, so nearly everything gets flagged 'changed' and the LiDAR outline gets adopted.
findings.fix: Use one-sided coverage ratios: the share of the polygon covered by the mask, and the share of each mask cell assigned to that polygon by nearest-polygon partition. Split mask components at roof-height breaks larger than about 3 m (part segmentation from M03) before matching. Count IoU only for free-standing buildings, then test the method on tile 490000_5459000 before adopting it.

findings.issue: The 2015 footprints were traced from orthophotos. Unless those were true orthophotos, relief displacement puts the roofs of 150 to 200 m towers several metres away from their bases. That breaks the '0.5 m edge error' target and makes the 2022 orthophoto QA step unreliable for towers. The 2022 orthophotos are also labelled EPSG:26910 (original NAD83), which sits about 1 m from NAD83(CSRS). PROJ may apply a ballpark transformation without warning.
findings.fix: For buildings taller than about 30 m, derive outlines from LiDAR building returns as the default, and use the City polygons only for low-rise. For QA, use LiDAR DSM hillshade rather than the orthophoto. Transform 26910 to 3157 with an explicit NTv2 or NAD83(CSRS) grid, and assert in a test that the transformation is not ballpark.

findings.issue: h_allow = H_cone minus Z_ground gives height above the 2022 bare-earth surface, interpolated under buildings. Vancouver zoning heights are measured from a bylaw base surface derived from building grades, not from a LiDAR DTM. Designers will read 'allowed height' as a zoning height. The cone datum, cone geometry and the 3.2.1 values (123.201 m, 361 ft) all remain unverified.
findings.fix: Make absolute maximum geodetic elevation (canonical datum) the primary output. Label any metres-above-ground figure 'above 2022 bare earth, not bylaw base surface'. Show sigma_allow next to it, and keep every on-screen value marked 'estimate' until views@vancouver.ca confirms the datum. Add a check that existing towers which pre-date cone amendments sit at or below the reconstructed H_cone, or are known exceptions.

findings.issue: The spec says 13 tiles lie within 2 km of downtown. Using the portal's 181 tile names, I count 20 tiles that intersect a 2 km radius around the Vista anchor (489000_5457000 to 493000_5459000). Scripted HEAD and GET requests to webtransfer.vancouver.ca/opendata/2022LiDAR/*.zip return HTTP 403, so the 'fetch only needed tiles' step cannot run unattended. Zips run up to 2.74 GB each, so 20 tiles may total tens of GB on a student laptop.
findings.fix: State the tile-selection rule and the list. Plan a manual browser download, with a sha256 manifest and file sizes recorded. Process one tile at a time with laspy chunking and delete the LAS afterwards. Measure real tile sizes before committing to the R0/R1 radii.

findings.issue: The module efforts add up to about 37 person-days (3+5+8+5+6+5+3+2). The course working core is due 13 Nov 2026, 23 calendar days from today, and the two students have other modules to build too. Several modules (LoD1.3 part clustering, multi-ring Delatin meshing, CI accuracy suite) are not needed for a first usable context model.
findings.fix: Define a minimum core for 13 Nov. (1) M01 registry with a datum statement. (2) M03 with a single p90/max height on 20 downtown tiles, no parts. (3) Terrain from City LiDAR 2 m plus MRDEM-30, single resolution per ring, as int16 tiles. (4) M06 tiling. Defer LoD1.3 parts, GLO-30, the Overture/NRCan cross-checks and the CI suite to v1.

findings.issue: The method computes PDAL p95 and max per 0.5 m cell, then takes zonal statistics. Percentiles of cell statistics are not percentiles of the point population that the 3D BAG benchmark uses, so the 0.31/1.06 m RMSE comparison is not like-for-like. The PDAL p<n> option itself is confirmed on the writers.gdal page.
findings.fix: Compute footprint percentiles directly from points (laspy plus a point-in-polygon index), or state the operator explicitly, e.g. 'P90 of 0.5 m cell maxima'. Cross-check the two on the synthetic-roof case.

findings.issue: The per-building cost of 982 B and 320 B leaves out the index JSON files: unified_buildings_index.json is 891,705 B and unified_ext_buildings_index.json is 4,534,560 B. Including them gives about 1,072 B and 408 B per building.
findings.fix: Benchmark against total shipped bytes per building, including indices and labels.

findings.item: C02-M05 metric 'Mountain DTM accuracy by source'
findings.issue: This metric is marked verified, but it pairs HRDEM's 'better than 1 m' with mountains that HRDEM does not cover (see the BLOCKER). The peak check also uses Wikipedia heights with an unstated datum.
findings.fix: Use the MRDEM GLO-30-derived vegetated figures for unconfirmed areas. Replace the peak check with GeoNetBC or NRCan control monuments on or near the summits where they exist.

findings.issue: The PROJ grid licence is listed as 'not stated' and meshoptimizer as 'unverified'. Both are determinable: PROJ-data ships a licence per agency directory, and meshoptimizer's repository LICENSE file is MIT.
findings.fix: Read the PROJ-data per-agency README/licence files (ca_nrc, us_nga) and the meshoptimizer LICENSE.md, then record them in layers.json.

findings.issue: City LiDAR is NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD (a BC realisation). NRCan COPC/HRDEM is NAD83(CSRS) epoch 2010. EPSG:10520 interpolates in NAD83(CSRS)v6. The difference is centimetre-level, but the registry treats them all as plain 'EPSG:3157'.
findings.fix: Record realisation and epoch for each layer. Measure any planimetric offset on building corners where City LiDAR and NRCan COPC (Lower_Mainland_2016) overlap downtown.

findings.issue: M04 gives Z_ground but no rule for origin eye height. A 2023 City memo, seen only as a search summary and not opened, describes the origin as the view of an average 5'6" (1.68 m) person.
findings.fix: Add origin Z = DTM at origin + eye height as a parameter, default 1.68 m, marked unverified until confirmed by the City.

false_assumptions.claim: HRDEM BC-Lower_Mainland_2016-1m (bbox to 49.5125 N) provides 1 m terrain and skyline for the North Shore front ranges (M05 R2; dataset row 'use').
false_assumptions.why_false: The bbox is an envelope. The project's extent polygon is a 334-vertex MultiPolygon that excludes the mountain peaks.
false_assumptions.correction: The North Shore peaks are not covered by any HRDEM project item returned for the area. Use MRDEM-30 (GLO-30-derived with forest removal) until other LiDAR coverage is confirmed.
false_assumptions.evidence: A point-in-polygon test on https://canelevation-dem.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/hrdem-lidar/BC-Lower_Mainland_2016-1m-extent.geojson gives: Grouse (-123.0817, 49.3803) outside, Seymour (-122.9444, 49.3933) outside, Crown, Cypress and the Lions outside; downtown, North Vancouver city and Capilano Lake inside. The Sunshine_Coast_2018 extent contains Hollyburn only. The Lower_Mainland_2019 extent contains none of them.

false_assumptions.claim: City LiDAR 2022 heights use the HTGVRDBC00 hybrid geoid (M01 limits; dataset table).
false_assumptions.why_false: The portal metadata names a different model file.
false_assumptions.correction: City LiDAR 2022: CGVD28GVRD, geoid HTMVBC00 (HTMVBC00_Abbbyn.zip). GeoBC calls HTMVBC00 equivalent to HTGVRDBC00 but extended east to Abbotsford. Record HTMVBC00.

false_assumptions.claim: Vista's frame differs from UTM by about 5 m at 2.5 km, which is fine for visuals; the difference is a generic projection effect.
false_assumptions.why_false: The main cause is a wrong latitude constant (110574 m/deg, the equatorial value), which shortens north-south distances by about 0.58% at 49.28 N. The supplied Rhino model fits this formula to 0.08 m, so it carries the same distortion.
false_assumptions.correction: Errors reach about 21 m at the north edge of the supplied downtown model and 27 to 34 m at the extension's southern corners. Treat Vista geometry as a distorted legacy frame.
false_assumptions.evidence: Computed with a Krueger transverse Mercator (GRS80, k0 0.9996, CM -123) checked against the City tile corner 490000_5459000 (reproduced to 0.0002 m). Vista offsets from UTM: (0, 3939.9) gives +6.3 E, +21.3 N; (5674.2, -5083.1) gives +5.8, -33.6. Formula from data/geo.json.

false_assumptions.claim: OGL-Vancouver may be 'viral' (share-alike), so City layers cannot be combined (M08 limits).
false_assumptions.why_false: That commentary dates from 2011 and predates the current licence. OGL-Vancouver is described as OGL-BC 2.0 with the province's name replaced, and OGL-BC 2.0 is attribution-only.
false_assumptions.correction: City layers need attribution only. The share-alike constraint comes from ODbL (OSM, Overture), so keeping OSM-derived layers separate is still right. Confirm the City's exact attribution string on the portal licence page, which my fetch could not render.
false_assumptions.evidence: Search summary of OSM talk-ca (2017) and help.openstreetmap.org/questions/59890; the portal licence page (https://opendata.vancouver.ca/pages/licence/) returned navigation only.

false_assumptions.claim: 13 City LiDAR 2022 tiles lie within 2 km of downtown.
false_assumptions.why_false: The tile-selection rule is undefined. Using the portal tile list, 20 tiles intersect a 2 km radius around the Vista anchor (E 491221.8, N 5458890.0).
false_assumptions.correction: State the rule and list the tiles: 489000-493000 E by 5456000-5460000 N (20 tiles intersect).

missing: Measured coverage map of 1 m LiDAR for the North Shore (HRDEM coverage.gpkg, LidarBC, Metro Vancouver watershed LiDAR, Districts of North and West Vancouver), and a fallback accuracy statement per view subject mountain.
A same-source datum bridge: City DEM 2013 (CGVD28) against HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER 2013 (CGVD2013), plus a GeoNetBC control-monument test.
Explicit transform and tests between Vista's legacy equirectangular frame and EPSG:3157, so old assets and estimated origins can be reused.
Rule for origin eye height and origin Z (DTM + 1.68 m, pending City confirmation).
Distinction between bylaw base-surface height and height above LiDAR bare earth in all user-facing outputs.
Validation of reconstructed cone heights against existing towers known to comply.
A minimum scope for the 13 Nov 2026 core, with the remaining 37 person-days of modules sequenced after it.
Manual-download procedure and checksum manifest for City LiDAR tiles (scripted access returns 403), plus measured tile sizes.
Outline-source policy for towers (LiDAR-derived by default above about 30 m) given likely orthophoto relief displacement.
Whether City 2015 and 2022 orthophotos are true orthophotos (affects footprint QA).

conditions: Replace the HRDEM North Shore claim with measured coverage, and restate mountain accuracy as MRDEM GLO-30-derived (about 5 m RMSE forested) wherever LiDAR is absent.
Correct the geoid entry to HTMVBC00 and record epochs. Add the same-source 2013 datum bridge and a sign-convention unit test for vgridshift.
Document Vista's 0.58% north-south scale error and require all comparisons in EPSG:3157.
Replace parcel-polygon IoU with one-sided coverage plus height-break segmentation, and test it on tile 490000_5459000.
Make absolute geodetic elevation the primary output, label above-ground values as non-bylaw estimates, and keep compliance wording blocked until the City confirms the cone datum.
Publish a reduced core plan that fits 13 Nov 2026.

Heights and years match the spec. Living Shangri-La is listed 2009 in the table but 2010 in the text; heights include spires and exclude antennas.
Page rendered navigation only; licence text unavailable.
403. Search summary: views are surveyed and GIS-modelled; origin based on an average 5'6" viewer; not all views have geodetic data.

Confirms SRTM 60 m/300 m EGM96, 9,897 + 51,510 buildings, height-source counts and a 51,990,003 B release. The equirectangular formula uses 110574 m/deg latitude. Index JSON files (0.89 MB and 4.53 MB) are omitted from the spec's per-building cost.

verdict: Not ready. The direction is sound: City LiDAR 2022 for downtown, a datum registry, LiDAR percentile heights and compact tiles. The tile corner, curvature and pixel-error figures check out. But the main terrain claim fails: no HRDEM project covers Grouse, Seymour, Crown, Cypress or the Lions, so the mountain profiles rest on GLO-30-derived MRDEM (about 5 m RMSE). Smaller problems: the geoid is mis-named (HTMVBC00), Vista's distortion is understated (it comes from a 0.58% north-south constant error, up to about 21 m inside the downtown model), parcel-polygon IoU breaks on contiguous podiums, and height above bare earth would be read as a zoning height. The effort (37 person-days) cannot fit before 13 Nov.
